title: ‘South Park’ Takes Bold Swipe At Donald Trump
text:
Hulton Archive/ Getty Images

“South Park” took a swipe at President Donald Trump by changing its name to “South America.”

The show’s creators revealed their new name in a cheeky post shared on social media on Tuesday.

“Following their Emmy win for Outstanding Animated Program, ‘South Park’ is making a big change.”“Inspired by the bravery and patriotism of Apple and Google, we are changing the name of South Park to SOUTH AMERICA,” they wrote.

A post shared by South America (@southpark)

Show writers Trey Parker and Matt Stone’s tongue-in-cheek rebrand for the upcoming 29th season mocks Trump’s push to replace geographic names with “America,” including the Gulf of Mexico becoming the “Gulf of America” and Lake Ontario being renamed “Lake America.”

Their social media post went on to say, “We especially want to thank our parent company Paramount — a Skydance Capitulation.”

The “Skydance Capitulation” comment jabs at the recent merger of Paramount and Skydance Media, underscoring Parker and Stone’s long-running friction with corporate executives. Whether the name change is permanent or just a temporary stunt, the move indicates they have no intention of backing down from controversy.

The series has also taken aim at Trump-era controversies involving ICE, the Epstein files and the administration’s relationship with powerful tech executives. (RELATED: Artists Abandon Jerry Seinfeld-Headlined Festival Over Political Tensions)

The show has relentlessly jabbed at Trump with its signature crude satire. They have depicted Trump in a relationship with Satan and mocked his penchant for lawsuits, while Vice President JD Vance has been portrayed as a childlike caricature.
